ra: Tarhunz is the chief storm-god of the Luwian pantheon.
Tiwaz is the Luwian sun-god.
Arma is the Luwian moon-god.
Runtiya is the Luwian stag/tutelary god.
Santa is a Luwian plague/war god.
Iyarri is the Luwian plague/war archer god.
Maliya is the Luwian goddess of rivers, gardens, and crafts.
Kubaba, the enthroned city-goddess, is a high deity of the Luwian (Iron Age Syro-Anatolian) pantheon.
'Kubaba of Carchemish' is the city-cult form of the goddess Kubaba, whose principal cult center was Carchemish.
Functional storm-sovereign cognate; in Syro-Anatolian Iron Age cult Tarhunz and Hurrian Teshub overlap as the supreme storm-god.
Storm-sovereign typological cognate; later interpretatio identifies the Anatolian storm-god (Zeus Dolichenus continuity) with Zeus.
Classic Kubaba > Kybebe > Cybele continuity: the Syro-Anatolian goddess Kubaba is the etymological and cultic forerunner of Phrygian/Greek Cybele (Burkert, West).
Luwian sun-god Tiwaz and Hittite sun-god Istanu are functional cognates (sun, justice, oaths).
Tiwaz aligns with the Hurrian sun-god Shimige as the regional sun/justice deity.
Luwian moon-god Arma and Hurrian moon-god Kushuh are functional cognates (moon, oaths).
Runtiya, the stag/hunt/wild-protection god, is the typological forerunner/cognate of the Anatolian Artemis (mistress of wild animals and the hunt).
Runtiya has been linked to Apollo in the Anatolian-tutelary-god discussion; offered low (the Artemis association is stronger).
Santa (Sanda) is attested in Anatolian-Mesopotamian syncretism with Marduk, sharing warrior/plague aspects.
Iyarri, the plague-bringing archer ('lord of the bow'), is the recognized Anatolian forerunner-type of the plague-archer Apollo (Smintheus).
Arma is the Luwian moon-god.
Maliya's domains include crafts (alongside rivers and gardens, the latter wired via ENT_WATER).
Iyarri is a plague-and-war god leading armies.
Santa is a plague-and-war god.
Tiwaz is the Luwian sun-god.
Tiwaz governs justice and oaths, the standard Anatolian sun-god judicial role.
Kubaba's domains include fertility/nature (pomegranate, lion iconography).
Kubaba functions as a city-protecting sovereign goddess.
Teshub is the Hurrian/Hittite chief storm-god, head of the imperial pantheon.
Tarhunna is the chief Hittite storm-god.
The Sun Goddess of Arinna is the chief state goddess of the Hittite pantheon.
Hepat is the Hurrian/Hittite queen of heaven, consort of Teshub.
Telipinu is a central Hittite vegetation/disappearing god.
Istanu is the Hittite sun-god of justice.
Kamrusepa is the Hittite goddess of magic and healing.
Kumarbi is the former king of the gods in the Hurrian-Hittite theogony.
Shaushka is the great Hurrian/Hittite love-and-war goddess (Ishtar-type).
Hannahanna is the Hittite mother/elder goddess of the Telipinu myth.
Alalu is the first divine king in the Hurrian-Hittite succession myth.
Sharruma is the son of Teshub and Hepat.
Lelwani is the Hittite underworld deity.
Halki is the Hittite grain/harvest god.
Kushuh is the Hurrian moon-god of oaths.
Shimige is the Hurrian sun-god of justice.
Wurunkatte is the Hattian/Hittite war-god.
Inara(s) is the Hittite protective/tutelary goddess of the Illuyanka myth.
Hutena and Hutellura are the Hurrian/Hittite goddesses of fate and birth.
Mezzulla, daughter of the Sun Goddess of Arinna, belongs to the Arinna cult.
Aranzah (the deified Tigris), son of Kumarbi, belongs to the Hurrian-Hittite pantheon.
Tashmishu, brother/vizier of Teshub, belongs to the Hurrian-Hittite pantheon.
Kumarbi-cycle succession: Teshub is born from Kumarbi (who swallowed Anu's seed).
Hepat is the standard consort of Teshub (the Hepat-Teshub pair).
Tashmishu is the brother and attendant of Teshub in the Kumarbi cycle.
Kumarbi fathers the stone monster Ullikummi (Song of Ullikummi) to overthrow Teshub.
The Kumarbi cycle's central conflict is Kumarbi's attempts to depose his son Teshub.
Istanu is the Hittite sun-god.
Istanu is the divine judge administering justice on his daily journey.
Kushuh is the Hurrian moon-god.
Shimige is the Hurrian sun-god.
Kamrusepa is the goddess of magic.
Kamrusepa is the goddess of healing incantations.
Lelwani rules the underworld and the dead.
Shaushka governs love and sexuality.
Shaushka governs war as well as love, the Ishtar-type dual domain.
Pumay (behind Pumayyaton/Pygmalion of Kition) is a Cypro-Phoenician deity; the single safe attested link given his uncertain function.
Lady of Byblos, head of the Byblos civic pantheon.
Egyptianizing iconography at Byblos led to her identification with Hathor.
Baal-Saphon is a Phoenician storm/sea cult-form; pantheon membership raises his degree without a false equation.
Sakon is an obscure Phoenician deity; pantheon membership is the safe additional link.
Shadrapa ('Shed has healed') is a Phoenician/Punic healing god.
In Punic Africa Shadrapa was equated with Liber/Dionysus (Latino-Punic dedications at Lepcis Magna).
Sid (eponym of Sardinia, temple of Antas) is a Punic hunt/war god.
Tanit was identified by Romans as Juno Caelestis (the celestial Juno), interpretatio Romana of the chief goddess of Carthage.
The dying-and-rising vegetation god Adonis of Byblos is the West-Semitic continuation/cognate of the Mesopotamian Dumuzi/Tammuz dying-shepherd complex.
Melqart of Tyre was identified with Heracles throughout the Greco-Roman world (Herodotus 2.44, the 'Tyrian Heracles').
Do-po-ta ('the Lord/Despotes'), a distinct Mycenaean titular deity at Pylos; pantheon membership, no Olympian equation.
i-pi-me-de-ja, a divine cult-recipient on PY Tn 316; pantheon membership.
pi-pi-tu-na, a pre-Greek/Minoan-substrate goddess on Knossos tablets; pantheon membership.
da-pu2-ri-to-jo po-ti-ni-ja, a distinct Cretan Potnia (KN Gg 702); pantheon membership.
qe-ra-si-ja, a distinct Cretan-Mycenaean cult name on Knossos tablets; pantheon membership.
ti-ri-se-ro-e ('Thrice-Hero'), hero/ancestor cult-recipient on PY Tn 316; pantheon membership.
di-u-ja, an independently worshipped Mycenaean goddess at Pylos (forerunner of Dione, not Hera); pantheon membership.
di-ri-mi-jo on PY Tn 316; pantheon membership is the safe link.
The di-wo i-je-we ('son of Zeus') reading on PY Tn 316 is plausible but rests on one line; offered LOW.
Distinct Mycenaean war deity, cult-recipient on PY Tn 316; pantheon membership.
e-nu-wa-ri-jo survives in Classical Greek chiefly as Enyalios; Enyo/Enyalios preserves the war-personification line.
Pantheon membership for the Etruscan messenger god.
Turms is the Etruscan Hermes/Mercury (messenger and psychopomp); the ancient-interpretatio equated_with form.
Pantheon membership for the two-faced gate-god.
Culsans is the two-faced Etruscan gate/threshold god, the direct counterpart of Janus (Cortona city gate).
Catha, a major celestial/light deity prominent at Pyrgi; pantheon membership (solar/lunar identity debated, no firm equation).
Cilens, a Liver-pantheon deity of debated function; pantheon membership.
Maris is a birth/rite divinity (NOT simply 'Mars'); pantheon membership, no false Mars equation.
Thalna, Etruscan goddess of childbirth and prophecy; pantheon membership.
Thanr, Etruscan birth/midwife goddess; pantheon membership.
Andrew and Simon Peter are brothers, sons of Jonah/John, called together by Jesus (Matt 4:18; John 1:40-42).
John and James the Greater are brothers, the sons of Zebedee ('Boanerges') (Matt 4:21; Mark 3:17).
Behemoth and Leviathan are the primordial land/sea chaos-monster pair (Job 40-41; 1 Enoch 60:7-9; 4 Ezra 6:49-52).
The Four Horsemen of Revelation 6 bring conquest and war (red horse 'to take peace from the earth').
The fourth Horseman is explicitly named Death, 'and Hades followed with him' (Rev 6:8).
As one of the Four Evangelists (Gospel-author), Matthew is a transmitter of the Gospel revelation.
Evangelist and Gospel-author, transmitter of the Gospel revelation.
Evangelist and Gospel-author, transmitter of the Gospel revelation.
Evangelist and Gospel-author; also the seer of the Book of Revelation.
